item.title: Litmus Music Secures $475M For More Catalog Acquisitions
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Litmus Music adds KKR backing as fresh capital expands the catalog buyer's reach across publishing and recorded music.
item.content:encoded:
Litmus Music is putting another $475 million behind its catalog-buying ambitions, adding KKR as an investor alongside longtime backer Carlyle.

The company already holds rights involving Juice WRLD, among other artists. Its new financing gives it more money to pursue additional catalogs, with Carlyle retaining majority ownership after the transaction.

In its announcement, Litmus described the money as capital commitments for acquisitions over the coming years. The firm has about $1.4 billion in assets under management, with a portfolio exceeding 100,000 copyrights and recordings.

“This investment marks an exciting next chapter for our company, providing meaningful additional capital to pursue new deals and accelerate growth,” CEO Hank Forsyth said.

Litmus’ connection to Juice WRLD predates this investment. In 2024, it bought Opus Music Group, whose holdings included rights associated with the late rapper, Maluma, Ozuna and Rauw Alejandro.

That purchase followed Opus’ earlier acquisition of a large stake in Juice WRLD’s catalog. Litmus financed the Opus transaction through a revolving credit facility that had been expanded to $400 million, according to reporting at the time.

The company had already bought compositions from benny blanco and rights tied to Katy Perry’s first five Capitol albums. Perry’s transaction covered her publishing and share of master royalty income, while Universal Music Group continued to own or control the recordings.

KKR brings its own history of buying into music. Its relationship with BMG dates to 2009, when it backed the company with 250 million euros to acquire publishing assets.

The two businesses joined forces again in 2021, with purchases involving music from John Legend and ZZ Top. KKR subsequently backed HarbourView Equity Partners through two $500 million asset-backed securitizations and bought European concert promoter Superstruct Entertainment.

Litmus also holds rights involving music by Randy Newman and Keith Urban.

Litmus’ founders also came through the record business. Forsyth worked at EMI, Warner Chappell and Blue Note, while co-founder Dan McCarroll led Capitol Records and later Warner Bros. Records.

Carlyle helped establish Litmus in 2022 with an initial $500 million commitment spanning equity and debt, alongside management’s investment.

KKR is funding its new investment primarily through its Asset-Based Finance Partners II fund.

item.title: YNW Melly Faces Prosecutors’ Challenge To Alibi Notice & Rap Evidence Motions
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: YNW Melly's pretrial calendar fills with fights over witnesses, digital records and attempts to exclude rap evidence.
item.content:encoded:
YNW Melly‘s alibi notice and effort to keep rap lyrics out of his murder retrial are headed for hearings as prosecutors ask a judge to strike several defense filings.

A two-page notice, electronically filed at 2:55 P.M. November 18 in Broward County, lays out seven matters the State plans to argue before Judge Martin Fein. Prosecutors are listed for November 20, 23 and 24, with hearings beginning at 9 A.M. in Courtroom 4780.

The agenda reaches beyond the gang-testimony dispute Melly’s attorneys raised last week. It also targets his supplemental witness list and a defense request to suppress material obtained through warrants involving an iPhone, Google, Snapchat and Instagram.

Those warrants were issued March 21, 2024, according to the notice, which appears in the Broward Clerk’s case records. The State identifies its requested action on that issue as striking the defense suppression motion.

Prosecutors also list a “Motion to Strike Defendant’s Alibi Notice” and a separate challenge to the supplemental witness list. The filing identifies the matters set for argument rather than presenting the State’s reasons for each request. The notice carries three prosecutors’ signatures.

The music-related dispute concerns the defense’s bid to exclude rap lyrics and videos. Another listed State motion challenges Melly’s effort to keep gang evidence and gang-expert testimony away from jurors.

Melly’s lawyers filed that gang-related request November 13. They argued that testimony at the first trial described alleged gang affiliations without connecting the material to the charged killings. Their eight-page filing focused on the risk that broad testimony about gang culture would prejudice jurors.

Timing-advance records are another contested category on the State’s hearing agenda. The docket shows a defense motion seeking their exclusion was also filed November 13.

A seventh matter concerns a State request to exclude testimony from Michelle Boutros and Kristine Bradley. The new notice dates that underlying motion to December 17, 2023.

Melly has pleaded not guilty to two first-degree murder charges stemming from the 2018 deaths of YNW Sakchaser and YNW Juvy. His first trial ended in a jury deadlock in July 2023.

The court’s hearing calendar lists his jury trial for January 6, 2027.

item.title: Suno Promises Artist-Likeness Filters As It Expands Into AI Music Videos
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Suno adds visual identity checks to its video push while Eminem's publishers pursue a separate fight over song copyrights.
item.content:encoded:
Suno is promising to keep artists’ faces out of unauthorized AI videos as it expands beyond music, with a copyright lawsuit from Eminem‘s publisher already on its plate.

The company introduced Visuals on November 17, allowing users to generate images and short videos around their songs.

In Suno’s announcement, chief product officer Jack Brody described filters intended to catch requests for depictions of specific performers, public figures and copyrighted material. Those checks cover both incoming prompts and uploads, the company says.

“This means that prompts that work on other video platforms may not work on Suno and that’s by design,” Brody wrote.

Suno says it also screens finished images and videos before users see them, adding outside tools to its own filters. Watermarks are supposed to travel with Visuals when users share them elsewhere.

The company’s musical output is already facing a different kind of challenge. As AllHipHop previously reported, Eight Mile Style and Martin Affiliated sued Suno over compositions from Eminem’s catalog.

Their November 6 complaint identifies 269 works and alleges Suno copied protected material without permission to develop its music-generation system. The publishers also accuse the service of producing lyrics and musical elements drawn from those compositions.

That case concerns songwriting copyrights, including the alleged use of songs during training and in generated output. The new Visuals announcement addresses another issue: whether a user can make an unauthorized image of a recognizable performer.

The complaint names the two publishing companies as plaintiffs and Suno as the defendant. Its allegations include copyright infringement, circumventing technological protections and removing copyright-management information.

Music Business Worldwide reported that Visuals runs on MiniMax’s H3 Move model. MiniMax is a Shanghai-based AI company listed in Hong Kong.

Among the songs named in the publishers’ complaint are “Stan,” “Lose Yourself” and “Without Me.” The companies say they control licensing rights to those works and never authorized their use for Suno’s training.

The publishers requested a jury trial in federal court in Northern California. Their complaint also asks for an injunction and an accounting of training data, scraping activities and datasets involving the compositions they say they control.

item.title: Isaiah Rashad Opens Up About Isolation After Touring
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Isaiah Rashad describes the struggle of going from packed shows to quiet days at home in a candid conversation about touring.
item.content:encoded:
Isaiah Rashad says coming home from tour left him feeling depressed within days, forcing him to recognize how much he missed being around people.

The Chattanooga rapper described that adjustment in an interview with The Truth Hurts, where the conversation turned to life away from the stage. Going from regular contact with crowds to spending time alone caught him off guard.

“I go from interacting with people every day to just not,” Rashad said.

At first, having time to himself felt welcome. Then he realized he needed to get out and talk to somebody. Rashad recalled attending a Jay-Z event because he wanted human contact after spending three days at home.

He linked the change in his mood to the affection and activity surrounding his performances. When the host suggested he might be chasing that feeling, Rashad pushed back. He described the contrast as something he was learning to understand.

The discussion also touched on meet-and-greets during the first leg of a tour.

“I’m more just surprised of like the drop off more than anything else,” Rashad said.

Rashad has spoken elsewhere about managing the expectations attached to his music. His recent discussion of pressure to represent recovery and queer communities focused on the weight of being treated as an example by listeners.

His album It’s Been Awful arrived five years after The House Is Burning, which came out in 2021. The newer project explored childhood and family experiences, with his brother Keem the Cipher serving as a lead producer.

Family has remained close to his work on the road. Keem lived and traveled with him, while Rashad also described his mother’s presence at important tour moments.

In a separate interview with The Village Voice, Rashad discussed building a life in Los Angeles while remaining connected to Chattanooga.

He called Los Angeles his second home and said he had spent much of the previous decade there.

His September 29 Anniversary Show at YouTube Theater celebrated several milestones: a decade of The Sun’s Tirade, 12 years of Cilvia Demo, and five years of The House Is Burning.

Rashad also told The Village Voice he was working on a deluxe edition of It’s Been Awful.

item.title: Travis Scott-Linked Company Drops Houston Comets Trademark Bid & Avoids War With WNBA
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Travis Scott's ties to a Houston company put him near a branding dispute that changed course ahead of the Comets' return.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Scott‘s Houston Comets trademark ties took a turn in October, when a company linked to him abandoned its application.

TSTM Holdings, a Delaware firm linked to the rapper, abandoned its Houston Comets trademark application on October 29, according to Front Office Sports. The outlet reviewed records documenting the move, which followed a filing made in 2024.

“I think the coast is now clear to move forward for the WNBA,” intellectual property attorney Jed Ferdinand told the outlet.

The league has since asked the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to advance its own application. Ferdinand said approval could still take months, with the WNBA required to demonstrate use of the name.

The dispute had already drawn attention to Scott’s business ties in his hometown. Chron reported in April that a source familiar with the matter confirmed his affiliation with TSTM.

The company uses attorney Kia Kamran, who has also represented Scott and LaFlame Enterprises. Chron noted that Delaware companies do not have to publicly identify their LLC members.

The WNBA challenged TSTM’s application in May 2025. Its opposition questioned whether the company genuinely planned to use the Comets branding, including pointing to a lack of merchandise.

Scott’s more visible relationship with Houston basketball stretches back years, including a Rockets clothing collaboration AllHipHop covered in 2017. That project put his handwritten version of the team’s playoff slogan, “Run As One,” on a limited-edition shirt.

The Rockets arranged to give the shirts to spectators attending Game 6 against the San Antonio Spurs at Toyota Center. Scott’s hometown appearance also coincided with a sold-out stop at Revention Music Center on his Birds Eye View Tour.

The Comets name carries its own history: Houston won the WNBA’s first four championships before the original franchise eventually closed in 2008. The returning team will use the Connecticut Sun’s roster after Tilman Fertitta’s purchase.

More recently, Scott and Drake attended the Rockets’ October 31 game against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The pair were then filmed in the audience at Ye’s Halloween concert at Houston’s Reliant Stadium later that same night.

The Comets unveiled their new logos on October 29.

item.title: Kia Shine Reveals The Shave And Secrecy Behind His GTA VI Role
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kia Shine describes the recording process that brought him into Rockstar's next game, with a surprising assist from his son.
item.content:encoded:
Kia Shine had to lose his beard and keep quiet about his work before he could tell Memphis about his role in “Grand Theft Auto VI.”

In an interview with WREG’s Alex Coleman, the rapper and actor described performance-capture sessions that required him to shave his facial hair. A headset recorded his movements, while repeated line readings kept him working until the director moved on.

“They don’t tell you it’s Grand Theft Auto,” Kia Shine said. “They tell you it’s Rockstar Games.”

He said the opportunity followed earlier work on “Red Dead Redemption 2” in 2018. His agent contacted him about the new project, and he booked the job in May of the previous year.

The secrecy even shaped how he learned where his work would appear. Kia Shine said his son recognized his voice in a trailer, prompting him to take a look himself.

Kia Shine said, “I shaved all of my beard, all of my mustache.” His daughter wanted the beard back after seeing his clean-shaven face at home.

The assignment adds another kind of production work to a career that began well before gaming entered the picture. In an earlier AllHipHop interview, Kia Shine explained how selling beats in New York led to a Ruff Ryders production deal and a publishing agreement with Universal.

He reinvested that money in his Memphis company, Rap Hustlers Music, which he ran with Jack Frost. Its roster included Yo Gotti, La Chat, Skinny Pimp and Gangsta Blac, giving him experience developing other artists before pushing his own records.

“Krispy” and “Respect My Fresh” helped establish his solo identity, followed by his Universal/Motown album “Due Season.” That history stretches from label operations and beatmaking to performing under somebody else’s direction for a game.

Rockstar’s official description places “Grand Theft Auto VI” in Leonida, with Jason and Lucia caught in a criminal conspiracy. Its music rollout includes an Atlantic Records soundtrack partnership and 34 original tracks, extending the game’s connection to recording artists beyond character performances.

Rockstar lists November 19 as the game’s release date for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

item.title: Wiley Convicted In Netherlands Over Antisemitic Posts, Campaign Group Says
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wiley's Dutch case ends in convictions without punishment, the group behind the complaint says, six years after his posts.
item.content:encoded:
Wiley has been convicted in the Netherlands over his antisemitic social media posts, but the court imposed no punishment because of the time that had passed, according to the organization that pursued the case.

Campaign Against Antisemitism announced the outcome on November 17, identifying the offenses as group defamation and incitement to violence under Dutch law.

The charity said Dutch prosecutors received its lawyers’ complaint after British police established that Wiley had been outside the U.K. when he posted the messages in July 2020.

The group said the messages attacked Jewish people collectively and called for violence. It credited Dutch lawyer Ronnie Eisenmann with pursuing the complaint and the Community Security Trust with helping establish Wiley’s location.

“He has now been convicted of group defamation and incitement to violence in The Netherlands,” said Stephen Silverman, the charity’s director of investigations and enforcement.

Wiley’s posts had already cost him professional relationships and access to major social platforms.

His longtime manager, John Woolf, ended their working relationship, and Facebook, Instagram and Twitter removed his accounts during the original controversy. Twitter also apologized for the time it took to respond before permanently suspending his account.

As AllHipHop reported at the time, Wiley later offered an apology while insisting the dispute should have stayed between him and his manager.

“My comments should not have been directed to all Jews or Jewish people,” Wiley said in an interview with Sky News.

“I’m not racist, you know. I’m a businessman,” he said.

The interview also included his offer to give up his MBE, an honor he had received for services to music in 2018, as calls grew for it to be withdrawn. “Take it back,” he said.

The East London MC helped build grime through Roll Deep, the crew that also included Dizzee Rascal before the two artists fell out.

Their relationship eventually improved enough for an onstage reunion at a Dubai concert in 2023.

“Antisemites do not stop at national borders and neither will we in pursuing them,” Silverman said when CAA announced its Dutch complaint in 2020.

Wiley later lost his MBE in February 2024, with the Cabinet Office citing bringing the honors system into disrepute.

item.title: Erica Campbell Hires Security After Unwanted Visits & Slashed Tires
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Erica Campbell says repeated visits to her home have prompted police calls and private security as she shares doorbell video.
item.content:encoded:
Erica Campbell says private security is part of her family’s response to repeated unwanted visits at their home, where she has shared footage of a woman at the door.

The Mary Mary singer has contacted the LAPD several times, according to TMZ, which reported on the videos and her account of the situation.

“I’m covered and protected, but I ain’t got no reason to lie to nobody for nothing,” Campbell wrote in her Instagram caption.

Her account includes a call from her daughter, who told her through FaceTime that a woman was in the backyard. Campbell said the visitor had appeared at the house before.

The videos described in the report show encounters at the entrance, including a woman attempting to communicate through a window. Campbell had previously told her church congregation that someone allegedly slashed the family’s tires.

She has described the situation as “not a joke” and “not a game,” while saying she has also sought help through mental health channels.

Campbell has spent much of her career bringing gospel into spaces shared with rap and R&B. Her recent work includes Skilla Baby’s “Strength in Numbers”, a song addressing poverty and violence on his album The Price of Fame.

That project arrived in August with other guests including Nas, Chris Brown and Bryson Tiller. Skilla has spoken about using the album to work through his own struggles after surviving a shooting.

David Banner also named Campbell among the collaborators on The God Box 2, alongside vocalists Anthony Hamilton, Raheem DeVaughn and Eric Bellinger. Those appearances extend a catalog that already reaches beyond her recordings with Mary Mary.

She and her sister Tina broke through with Thankful in 2000. Campbell later established a solo career with Help, which debuted atop the Top Gospel Albums chart and reached No. 6 on the Billboard 200.

Her first solo single, “A Little More Jesus,” earned a Grammy nomination before that album arrived.

The song also earned writing nominations for Tina and Warryn, keeping the family’s creative partnership intact even as Campbell stepped out with her own solo material.

Campbell and her husband, producer Warryn Campbell, married in 2001.

item.title: Wyclef Jean & Lauryn Hill Bring Clipse To Brooklyn For ‘The Score’ Anniversary
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wyclef Jean and Lauryn Hill book Brooklyn with Clipse, family ties and a ticket donation attached to The Score's anniversary.
item.content:encoded:
Wyclef Jean and Lauryn Hill are bringing “The Score” back to Brooklyn, with Clipse opening their December 17 anniversary concert at Barclays Center.

For Hill, the location connects the Fugees’ music to family history and a departed friend. She explained that connection in a statement announcing the show.

Hill said: “Brooklyn is woven into our story. It’s where my mother was born, where Wyclef first landed after leaving Haiti, and where our brother John Forté, RIP, called home. There’s something about Brooklyn that has always resonated with us: its spirit, its people, its music, and its ability to uniquely reflect culture while moving the world. The love has always been mutual, and we’ve never forgotten that. Brooklyn in the ’90s was something else! We’re beyond excited to celebrate this anniversary in Brooklyn.”

The one-night event celebrates 30 years of the Fugees’ second album. Pusha T and Malice will perform as Clipse, with additional guests still to be announced.

“Thirty years on, The Score still sounds past, present and future,” Wyclef said. “We made a vow to ourselves as teenagers that music is only the byproduct of the movement. We said we would be the voice of the voiceless. Young or old, we will forever cross generations. That’s what a classic does. It doesn’t age, it just keeps finding new ears. Our job is to make sure the world keeps hearing it, and that the next generation gets to discover it for the first time.”

The Brooklyn booking follows the pair’s announced Miami Art Week appearance, extending a run built around the album. Their anniversary performances have already included Lisbon and Paris.

Released in 1996, “The Score” brought “Ready or Not,” “Fu-Gee-La” and “Killing Me Softly” to a worldwide audience. The Fugees won two Grammys the following year, including Best Rap Album. The album also reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

Organizers say tickets go on sale November 19 at 10 A.M. Eastern through Ticketmaster. The December 17 performance is scheduled for 8 P.M., with Jay Upscale and Global Citizen partnering on the event.

One dollar from each ticket will go to the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund.

item.title: Camp Flog Gnaw Gets Praise & Plenty Criticism
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Camp Flog Gnaw’s value gets questioned after alleged repetitive performances, merchandise overload and Tyler's large security.
item.content:encoded:
I promise. This is the top level of what a source conveyed. My editor’s said, “No” to revealing everything seen and said.

Tyler, The Creator might want to check the Camp Flog Gnaw suggestion box. A source close by said the carnival may want to get some new rides.

The festival returned to Dodger Stadium on November 14 and 15, but an attendee who spoke with AllHipHop says Saturday left them questioning whether the experience still justified the expense.

READ ALSO: Tyler, The Creator’s Sold-Out Camp Flog Gnaw Streams Live…

“It was pretty much just a money grab,” the source said. They were a VIP too.

Whew.

Don Toliver’s performance was among their biggest grievances. The source said one song came around five times, as in he performed the same song consecutively. Admittedly, others that reviewed the show did not have that experience. Same festival, very different ride home. It also may be an age thing. I dunno.

There were bright spots. Leon Thomas and JID were praised and apparently got all the audience engagement too. Glad to hear they had the chutzpah to serve all in attendance.

Then came the complaints about the grounds. If you were not buying a lot, you may not have been interested, because the merchandise presence was heavy, They could not locate the journalist interview area at all.

“And if it was if it existed, I don’t know where the hell it was,” the source said.

The credentials may have changed, or something or maybe they deliberately excluded journalists. We do not know since we were not there.

Tyler is a star. This is the part I am not so sure about. Tyler was not so close to fans and those that adore him. He was not so readily available and surrounded by a lot of security.

READ ALSO: Freddie Gibbs And Alchemist Have Another Helping Of Alfredo On The Way…

“I mean I guess it means he’s a human being,” they said.

Let’s get to the ticket prices. The official website lists starting prices of $415 for general admission, $725 for VIP and $1,750 for Super VIP. Lawdie. I’d definitely be sitting outside of the venue and try to hear some stray sounds.

Has Camp Flog Gnaw become so polished as a shopping destination that some fans are missing the gathering they originally loved? That’s what I am gathering and I can relate. We were front line on stuff like The Roots Picnic and AfroPunk. Not a shred of hate, but they are very different now than when they started.

Hip-Hop fans will buy the shirt. A journalist or an industry person may not. That may be the big difference here.
